cards.anchor: Achieve the bounded synthetic outcome: three elevation-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent when sampling starts at second 120. One stipulated continuous 300 rpm trial already met this proxy at approximately 2.4 percent after stopping at second 60; it does not establish reliable success of either proposed schedule or a concurrency mechanism.
cards.burden: Six fresh trials comprise three pairs within the 90-minute limit. Each arm requires 60 commanded stirring seconds, three 10 mL withdrawal-return cycles and manual five-second imaging. Staggering adds no commanded stirring or transfer dose, but retains a 105-second operation window. Savings relative to the preferred rule are unestablished. Keep the spill tray in use and stop if liquid escapes.
cards.construction: In both arms command nominal 300 rpm at seconds 0-15, 30-45, 60-75 and 90-105, commanding zero between intervals. Perform three marked low-position 10 mL withdrawals and upper-side returns, each completed within five seconds. The coupled arm transfers at 10-15, 40-45 and 70-75; the staggered arm transfers at 25-30, 55-60 and 85-90, after ten commanded-off seconds. Use fresh prescribed 150 mL water plus 0.30 mL dye, rinsed vessel, fixed addition location, one dye bottle and locked camera per comparison block. Finish at 105, retain fifteen quiet seconds, then withdraw 1 mL at each marked 10, 28 and 45 mm depth within ten seconds from 120.
cards.defeat: Reproducible staggered target failures paired with coupled successes defeat the proposed dispensability of commanded overlap for these doses. Both arms failing leave this opening unresolved. Staggered success cannot prove that actual fluid rotation and redistribution never overlapped.
cards.mutation: Replace the hypothesized necessary temporal interface between rotation and redistribution with a staged composition: retain both parent doses and move only the three transfer windows into commanded-off intervals. Optical spread is recorded and never controls operation.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: commanded concurrency is dispensable for this bounded composition. Staggered trials would reproducibly meet the at-most-4-percent depth-vial target, including all three repeats if the account holds under these conditions. Success of both arms would challenge concurrency necessity without identifying the mixing mechanism.
cards.prediction_rival: Hypothesis: the given doses achieve the target because transfers act during commanded rotation. Coupled trials would reproducibly pass while staggered trials exceed 4 percent. That pattern would favor the coupled schedule, while leaving transfer timing and residual flow as alternative explanations.
cards.probe: Run three fresh coupled/staggered pairs, reversing arm order across pairs and alternating depth-sampling order within pairs. Check water-only and common-aliquot references per block. Record raw vial attenuation and normalized spread, sampling order, commanded speeds, start/stop times, transfer times and counts, five-second side-region spread, surface depression and speck-containing frame counts. Compare paired target attainment and every failure. Matching parent doses and final quiet interval isolates commanded transfer timing as the intervention; it does not isolate actual hydrodynamic overlap. Stable images cannot substitute for vial success.
cards.rival: Concurrent rotation may make low-to-high transfers more effective at redistributing dye than identical transfers during commanded-off windows; an equal-dose sequence may therefore miss the target.
unknowns: Both proposed schedules and their successes remain unobserved; three pairs provide limited replication.
Ten commanded-off seconds do not verify stopped fluid motion; no independent tachometer measures actual speed.
Changing transfer times also changes dye age and subsequent stirring exposure; paired differences cannot uniquely establish a concurrency mechanism.
Sampling and transfers can disturb gradients. Common-aliquot repeatability does not supply concentration calibration.
Bright specks do not identify bubbles; their causal role remains unknown. This probe needs no absent bubble or absolute-concentration instruments.
Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit follows from the proxy.
